title: AfD Overtakes CDU in Polls for First Time: 28% vs 24% — Coalition Survival Doubted
detail: An INSA poll published the week of May 4 showed the AfD at 28% — ahead of the CDU at 24% — for the first time in German polling history. The SPD stood at 13.5%. Three-quarters of respondents said the Merz coalition government was failing, and 58% predicted it would not survive until 2029. The poll reflected deep public discontent with both the CDU-SPD coalition's welfare reform disputes and the Merz government's handling of the US troop withdrawal crisis. The AfD's new polling lead came despite the Constitutional Court's ongoing proceedings regarding the domestic intelligence agency's 'extremist' classification of the party.

media.caption: INSA May 2026 poll: AfD 28% leads CDU 24%, first time AfD has polled ahead of CDU

title: Trump Threatens to Cut Troops 'A Lot Further' and Impose 25% EU Car Tariffs
detail: Following the May 1 announcement of 5,000 US troop withdrawals from Germany, President Trump escalated the dispute on May 2, stating the reduction would go 'a lot further than 5,000.' Trump simultaneously threatened to raise EU automobile and truck tariffs from 15% to 25%, a move estimated to cost Germany's automotive sector nearly $18 billion. The tariff threat targeted Germany's largest export sector — cars from BMW, Mercedes-Benz, Volkswagen, and Audi. European allies expressed alarm at what NBC News analysts called a 'disastrous trend' in transatlantic relations.

media.caption: Trump threatens deeper troop cuts and 25% EU car tariffs, escalating feud with Chancellor Merz
